title: Hugging Face Hub
subtitle: I published a 4-bit quantization of a 27-billion-parameter model with its card, provenance and measured trade-off.

stats.label: tensors left bit-identical to the source
files checked on the uploaded copy

lede: ActiveKV needed a 27-billion-parameter model on one 32 GB Intel Arc Pro GPU, and the hybrid recurrent-attention open-weight model I chose does not fit on it in BF16. I decided to quantize it myself on Intel's stock XPU vLLM build, measure the trade-off, and publish the result on the Hugging Face Hub so anyone with an Intel Arc Pro GPU could run it. The recipe is weight-only W4A16 on the text projection modules, with every other tensor bit-identical to the source. I pinned the source to a revision and checked every shard hash, and a per-module manifest lists what was quantized. I skipped calibration, so the checkpoint can be reproduced from the source weights alone.
quote: I ran the release checks on the bytes that were uploaded, because a copy step can change them.
evidence: LLM quantization (4-bit): a W4A16 build of a 27-billion-parameter model, 400 modules quantized and 799 tensors bit-identical, 55.6 GB to 20.6 GB, +36% throughput for +3.33% perplexity.
Model release engineering: a published model card with method, tested environment and untested areas, and release checks run on the uploaded copy across 433 files.
Human-approved model acquisition: agents plan a download and only a person at the local console approves it, with registration in a single transaction.
author: Corey James
